# STD-TEC-NXT-001: Next.js Coding Standards

**Standards Metadata**

```yaml
standard_id: 'STD-TEC-NXT-001'
standard_name: 'Next.js Coding Standards'
standard_type: 'technology'
category: 'technology'
version: '1.0.0'
status: 'active'
compliance_level: 'mandatory'
tags: ['technology', 'nextjs', 'coding', 'typescript', 'mandatory']
```

---

> This document defines the coding standards for Next.js development within enterprise environments. These standards ensure consistent, maintainable, and performant React applications with proper TypeScript usage, component organization, state management, and Next.js-specific patterns.

[standards/technology/nextjs/STD-TEC-NXT-001-coding.md#10-overview]

## 1.0 Overview

This document defines the coding standards for Next.js development within enterprise environments. These standards ensure code quality, readability, maintainability, and consistency across all Next.js-based frontend applications.
page_texts.8:
[standards/technology/nextjs/STD-TEC-NXT-001-coding.md#23-naming-conventions]

### 2.3 Naming Conventions

-   **Interfaces/Types**: Use PascalCase
-   **Variables/Functions**: Use camelCase
-   **Constants**: Use UPPER_SNAKE_CASE for true constants
-   **Components**: Use PascalCase
-   **Files**: Use kebab-case for page files, PascalCase for component files
page_texts.13:
[standards/technology/nextjs/STD-TEC-NXT-001-coding.md#33-functional-components]

### 3.3 Functional Components

-   Use functional components with hooks instead of class components
-   Use named function exports for components, not anonymous arrow functions
-   Export components as default when they are the main component in a file
page_texts.14:
[standards/technology/nextjs/STD-TEC-NXT-001-coding.md#34-state-management]

### 3.4 State Management

-   Keep state as local as possible
-   Use React Query for server state
-   Use Context API or state management libraries for shared state
-   Split complex state logic into custom hooks
page_texts.15:
[standards/technology/nextjs/STD-TEC-NXT-001-coding.md#35-component-styling]

### 3.5 Component Styling

-   Use CSS Modules for component-scoped styles
-   Follow the naming convention `ComponentName.module.css`
-   Use Tailwind CSS for utility classes when appropriate
-   Consider styled-components or Emotion for dynamic styling needs
page_texts.17:
[standards/technology/nextjs/STD-TEC-NXT-001-coding.md#41-app-router-vs-pages-router]

### 4.1 App Router vs Pages Router

-   Use the App Router for all new projects
-   Follow the nested layout pattern for shared UI
-   Use the recommended file conventions (page.tsx, layout.tsx, loading.tsx, error.tsx)
page_texts.20:
[standards/technology/nextjs/STD-TEC-NXT-001-coding.md#44-routing-and-navigation]

### 4.4 Routing and Navigation

-   Use the Link component for client-side navigation
-   Use route groups (folders in parentheses) to organize routes without affecting the URL path
-   Implement proper route-based code splitting
page_texts.21:
[standards/technology/nextjs/STD-TEC-NXT-001-coding.md#45-layout-and-templates]

### 4.5 Layout and Templates

-   Use layouts for shared UI across routes
-   Use templates when you need a new instance of the UI wrapper on navigation
page_texts.22:
[standards/technology/nextjs/STD-TEC-NXT-001-coding.md#46-api-routes]

### 4.6 API Routes

-   Implement API routes in the app/api directory
-   Use proper request validation and error handling
-   Follow RESTful principles for endpoint design
-   Use appropriate HTTP methods and status codes
page_texts.24:
[standards/technology/nextjs/STD-TEC-NXT-001-coding.md#51-local-component-state]

### 5.1 Local Component State

-   Use `useState` hook for simple state
-   Use `useReducer` for complex state logic
-   Extract reusable state logic into custom hooks
page_texts.26:
[standards/technology/nextjs/STD-TEC-NXT-001-coding.md#53-global-state-management]

### 5.3 Global State Management

-   Use Zustand or Jotai for global state management
-   Split state into logical domains (auth, ui, data)
-   Follow the principle of least privilege for state access
page_texts.28:
[standards/technology/nextjs/STD-TEC-NXT-001-coding.md#61-code-splitting]

### 6.1 Code Splitting

-   Leverage Next.js automatic code splitting
-   Use dynamic imports for large components or libraries
-   Implement proper loading states for dynamically imported components
page_texts.29:
[standards/technology/nextjs/STD-TEC-NXT-001-coding.md#62-image-optimization]

### 6.2 Image Optimization

-   Use the Next.js Image component for all images
-   Specify proper width, height, and loading strategy
-   Use appropriate image formats (WebP, AVIF)
page_texts.30:
[standards/technology/nextjs/STD-TEC-NXT-001-coding.md#63-static-generation-vs-server-side-rendering]

### 6.3 Static Generation vs Server-Side Rendering

-   Use Static Generation (SSG) for content that doesn't change frequently
-   Use Server-Side Rendering (SSR) for personalized or frequently updated content
-   Consider hybrid approaches for different parts of the page
page_texts.31:
[standards/technology/nextjs/STD-TEC-NXT-001-coding.md#64-incremental-static-regeneration]

### 6.4 Incremental Static Regeneration

-   Use ISR for pages that change occasionally
-   Set appropriate revalidation intervals
-   Implement on-demand revalidation for content updates
page_texts.32:
[standards/technology/nextjs/STD-TEC-NXT-001-coding.md#70-testing-standards]

## 7.0 Testing Standards

See [Next.js Testing Standards](./STD-TEC-NXT-006-testing.md) for detailed testing guidelines.
page_texts.34:
[standards/technology/nextjs/STD-TEC-NXT-001-coding.md#81-component-documentation]

### 8.1 Component Documentation

-   Document components with JSDoc comments
-   Include descriptions for props, return values, and side effects
-   Add usage examples when appropriate

```typescript
/**
 * Button component with various styles and sizes.
 *
 * @param {ButtonProps} props - Component properties
 * @param {string} props.variant - Visual style of the button (primary, secondary, ghost)
 * @param {string} props.size - Button size (small, medium, large)
 * @param {ReactNode} props.children - Button content
 * @param {() => void} props.onClick - Click handler function
 * @param {boolean} [props.disabled] - Whether the button is disabled
 * @example
 * <Button variant="primary" size="medium" onClick={handleClick}>
 *   Click Me
 * </Button>
 */
```
page_texts.35:
[standards/technology/nextjs/STD-TEC-NXT-001-coding.md#82-api-documentation]

### 8.2 API Documentation

-   Document API routes with clear descriptions
-   Include request/response types and examples
-   Document error scenarios and status codes
page_texts.36:
[standards/technology/nextjs/STD-TEC-NXT-001-coding.md#90-accessibility-standards]

## 9.0 Accessibility Standards

-   Follow WCAG 2.2 AA standards
-   Implement proper semantic HTML elements
-   Provide appropriate ARIA attributes
-   Ensure keyboard navigation works correctly
-   Test with screen readers
page_texts.37:
[standards/technology/nextjs/STD-TEC-NXT-001-coding.md#100-deployment-and-build-process]

## 10.0 Deployment and Build Process

-   Optimize builds with appropriate Next.js configuration
-   Implement proper environment variable management
-   Use the recommended deployment platforms (Vercel, AWS, Azure)
-   Set up proper CI/CD pipelines for automated deployments
